newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn sets contract lows on excellent weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn sets contract lows on excellent weather.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower and contract lows were set in most months with excellent crop weather in the U.S. Midwest again hitting the market, traders said.

"It's getting to be old hat, contract lows again. It's mostly weather and in fact everything looks fantastic, it's getting close to pollination and no problems yet," said Tom Levis, analyst for Prudential Securities.

The new contract low for new-crop December is $2.27-1/2, below the previous low of $2.31-3/4 set Wednesday. Nearby July reached a session low of $2.40, equal to its contract low of $2.40 set one week ago.
Traders said the market remained overwhelmed with the mild temperatures and occasional rainfall in the key U.S. corn growing states.

Some analysts are citing a potential 10.0-billion-bushel corn crop this year, assuming the weather remains conducive for the key pollination and ear-filling stage of the plant's development. A record 10.1 billion bushels were produced in 1994.
Corn closed 1/4 to 4-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with July down 4-1/4 at $2.40-1/2. December was down four at $2.29-1/4.

USDA late Monday was expected to reveal another hike in the condition rating for the U.S. corn crop. A week ago the crop was 74 percent good to excellent, above the 67 percent in that category the previous week.

Export news failed to generate buying interest with USDA Monday pegging U.S. export inspections for corn during the week ending July 3 at 20.288 million bushels. There were expectations for the tally to be from 24 million to 30 million bushels.

Funds sold roughly a net 11.0 million bushels with Griffin Trading a key seller of 10.0 million bushels of December, traders said. Refco Inc and Prudential Securities each sold five million December, traders said.

E.D. and F. Man International bought four million bushels of December, Farmers Commodities Corp and Continental Grain each bought three million December and R.J. O'Brien bought two million bushels of December, traders said.

In spread trading, Continental Grain did two million bushels of December/September at 1/4 cent, premium September, traders said. Cargill Inc spread 1.5 million bushels of December/March at 8-1/4 cents, premium March, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 60,000 contracts, above the 39,074 traded Thursday.
In corn options, Griffin Trading bought 1,500 December $2.50 puts at 24-1/2 to 25 cents, E.D. and F. Man International sold 750 December $2.90 puts at 62 to 62-1/4 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 15,000 contracts, slightly below the 15,690 traded Thursday.
